submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on an evaluative quality adjective (by far most strongly ' good'/' Good'; weaker for ' bad', ' great', ' successful', ' poor', ' excellent', ' happy', ' decent', ' strong') when it sits in a generic or normative frame about what makes something a good instance of its kind, e.g. 'the key/secret to a good X', 'what makes a good X', 'a/every good X should/must', 'to be/do a good X', 'how to become a good X', 'you need a good X', 'Good food tastes better'. It stays near zero on the same adjective when it evaluates a particular, episodic referent ('She was a good teacher', 'It was a good movie', 'He did a good job', 'had a good time'), in predicate position ('the food was good'), in fixed phrases ('a good idea', 'Good morning'), and on non-evaluative adjectives (new, long, famous, local).
